There is no requests-per-minute quota. Cached input tokens read through prompt caching do not count against the input-tokens-per-minute quota, which is one more reason caching helps at scale. If a token-per-minute quota is exceeded, the endpoint returns an HTTP 429 response. Handle transient throttling with exponential backoff and a bounded retry count, which the OpenAI SDK supports through its `max_retries` setting. For more information, refer to Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint.\\\\n\\\\nOne recommended way to handle transient throttling is exponential backoff with a bounded retry count. They expire automatically (maximum 12 hours) and inherit the permissions of the IAM role that generated them. {"id": "a85c8e02-58b8-4d61-aa2b-63a775c1437d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes. The `-mantle-` in that usage type means the requests were billed as `bedrock-mantle` endpoint traffic. The input-token quota for that endpoint is the one that applies to you.

**Why the usage type tells you this**
- The Bedrock docs on Cost and Usage Report data list `{region}-{model}-mantle-{token-type}-standard` as the format for `bedrock-mantle` requests. The `bedrock-runtime` formats don't include `mantle`.
- Your line, `USE1-anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-mantle-input-tokens-standard`, matches that format. It is us-east-1, input tokens, standard tier, on the mantle endpoint.
- The docs' own example is `USE1-openai.gpt-oss-120b-mantle-input-tokens-standard`.

**Which quota applies**
- `bedrock-mantle` has its own quotas, separate from `bedrock-runtime`. They are per model, per Region: input tokens per minute and output tokens per minute.
- In Service Quotas, open Amazon Bedrock and search for "Bedrock Mantle". The quota is named "Bedrock Mantle input tokens per minute for <model>". The name you quoted, "[bedrock-mantle endpoint] Input tokens per minute", is probably how the console shows it for your model.
- Check the output-tokens-per-minute quota too, because it is a separate limit.

**Things to know**
- The input quota is shared across every API the endpoint serves for that model. That covers the Anthropic Messages API, OpenAI Chat Completions and OpenAI Responses.
- Cached input tokens read through prompt caching don't count against the input quota.
- The endpoint has no requests-per-minute quota. Throttling comes only from the token quotas, and you'll see HTTP 429s when you exceed them.
- When a request is admitted, the input check counts your input tokens plus the requested `max_tokens`. The unused part is released when the response completes. A high `max_tokens` can therefore cause throttling even when your actual input is modest.
- Any Claude Sonnet 5 traffic that goes through `bedrock-runtime` (InvokeModel or Converse) is billed under different usage types, without `mantle`. It is governed by the runtime quotas, such as the cross-Region TPM quotas. If you use both paths, the runtime lines will show up separately in Cost Explorer.

I didn't check the live quota values or your CloudWatch metrics for the endpoint. I can look at those if you're investigating throttling.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
